commentary.text: I’m claiming a central square immediately with Red, beginning a coordinated center-occupation threat while preserving flexible lanes for Yellow.
I’m taking a central foothold while blocking Yellow’s direct route up column 3. The piece is not currently exposed to an immediate sandwich.

I’m securing (3,4) with Yellow to deny Blue easy access to that central square. Together with Red at (3,3), this controls half the center and leaves Yellow’s route toward (4,4) open for a later occupation threat.
I’m mobilizing Green onto column 4 to pressure the remaining center square and create a future vertical capture anchor, while keeping the Green piece on row 4 available behind Blue’s blockade.
I’m using the vacated top-edge square to make a certain legal correction while keeping Red’s formation intact.
I’m placing a Blue anchor above Yellow’s central piece. This creates a sandwich threat through column 4 and supports our Green advance toward the lower-right center.

I’m placing Yellow at (4,2), creating a direct sandwich threat against Blue on (4,3): Yellow at (3,4) can move to (4,4) next turn and capture it. This also builds pressure around the center without vacating our current central square.

Yellow’s move threatens to use the open lower-right center as the landing flank against Blue. I’m occupying that square now, denying the immediate sandwich and securing both lower central squares for our team.

I’m creating a second threat against Blue: Red on (2,5) will let the central Red move to (2,3) and sandwich Blue at (2,4). Blue must also address Yellow’s existing double-capture threat along row 4, so this fork should force a material or positional concession.

Red’s new piece also pressures our upper Blue anchor, but Yellow has a more immediate two-piece sandwich available on row 4. I’m opening a gap in that line while keeping Blue directly beneath the center to deny Yellow access up column 3.
I’m advancing Yellow onto (4,3), taking a third central square and directly constraining Green’s central piece. This creates a persistent center-win threat while keeping Yellow at (3,4) in place.

Yellow stepped between two Green positions, allowing an immediate same-color sandwich. I’m closing it now to remove Yellow from the lower-left center, break Team A’s three-square occupation, and relieve the pressure on Blue below.
I’m cashing in the prepared Red sandwich: moving beside the Red anchor at (2,5) captures Blue at (2,4). This gains material while leaving Yellow at (3,4) to contest the center.

With Red vacating the upper-left center, Blue can occupy it safely and turn the remaining Yellow center piece into a direct sandwich target against our Blue on the right. Yellow must now retreat or risk capture.

I’m reinforcing the exposed Yellow center piece by moving another Yellow to (3,5), blocking Blue’s prepared sandwich from the right. This preserves our foothold at (3,4) and gives the Yellow formation more flexibility around the center.

Yellow has extended the row-3 line, creating a potential two-piece Blue sandwich. Meanwhile, I’m claiming the vacant lower-left center: Team B now holds three central squares and keeps strong pressure on Yellow’s remaining central piece.

I’m blocking Blue’s immediate move from (3,7) to (3,6), which would sandwich both central Yellow pieces against Blue at (3,3) and eliminate Yellow. Red now occupies that critical endpoint while adding pressure beside the center.

Red’s blocking move prevents the row-3 capture, but it left the other Red piece directly between two Blue positions on column 3. I’m exploiting that sandwich immediately while preserving our three-square center hold.

I’m blocking Green’s immediate route from (2,0) to (2,4), which would sandwich Yellow at (3,4) against Green at (4,4). Keeping that Yellow in place is essential because vacating or losing control of (3,4) exposes a Team B center win.

Red is poised to attack Blue on column 3, so I’m developing Green beside the advanced Yellow piece. This creates a direct next-turn route to land at (2,2) and sandwich that Yellow against Green on the edge, forcing it to react.

I’m taking the available Red sandwich: the move to (2,3) uses Red at (0,3) as the far flank and captures Blue at (1,3), bringing Blue to two losses. It also places Red directly above the contested center while preserving Yellow’s blockade on Green’s row-2 route.

Blue must avoid any further loss, so I’m withdrawing the blocked edge piece to a safe square while creating a concrete threat: from row 1 it can return to column 3 and sandwich Red at (2,3) against our central Blue.

I’m placing Yellow at (4,5) as the far flank for a future row-4 sandwich. If we can bring another Yellow to (4,2), the two central Green pieces can be captured together; meanwhile Yellow at (3,4) remains fixed to prevent Team B’s immediate center victory.
Yellow left the edge piece in the sandwich threat. I’m completing it now, taking Yellow to two losses and placing Green near Red’s advanced piece without disturbing our three-square center control.

I’m taking the clean sandwich on Green at (2,2), using Red at (2,3) as the far flank. This also creates a tactical trap: if Blue captures that Red from row 1, the new Red at (2,1) can later return to (2,3) and sandwich Blue against the Red anchor at (0,3), delivering Blue’s third loss.

I’m preserving Blue’s final life while creating an elimination threat against Yellow. From (1,5), Blue can descend to (3,5) and sandwich the central Yellow against Blue at (3,3), so Yellow must disrupt that line.

I’m repositioning the rear Yellow from (7,3) to (7,2), opening a clear route to (4,2). That threatens to sandwich both central Green pieces on row 4 against Yellow at (4,5), forcing Team B to break up its center formation or concede two captures.

Yellow ignored Blue’s elimination threat, so I’m adding a second one on the other Yellow piece. Green on (6,6) can rise to (4,6) and sandwich Yellow at (4,5) against Green at (4,4), leaving Red unable to cover both capture routes alone.

I’m occupying (3,5) with Red to stop Blue’s immediate move there, which would sandwich Yellow at (3,4) against Blue at (3,3) and eliminate Yellow. This preserves our center defense and leaves Yellow’s threat to capture both central Green pieces intact.

Red has blocked the immediate elimination square, so I’m advancing Blue onto (2,5). This safely pins the blocker’s upward route and builds a vertical line for future pressure while Green’s separate threat still forces Yellow at (4,5) to move.

I’m executing the prepared row-4 sandwich: Yellow moves to (4,2), flanking the two Green center pieces against Yellow at (4,5). Capturing both raises Green from one loss to three and eliminates it, breaking Team B’s central formation while keeping our Yellow center piece protected.

Although Green is now Void, it can still serve as a blocker. I’m placing it at (3,6), sealing Red’s only open escape from column 5; this preserves Blue’s next move to (5,5), which sandwiches both Yellow and Red against Blue at (2,5).

I’m placing Red at (3,1) to tighten the net around Blue’s last central piece. Yellow threatens to capture it from (4,2) via (3,2); if Blue sidesteps onto (3,2), Red can finish the sandwich next turn, while moving down abandons the center and remains tactically constrained.
The blocking Void held the column-5 line intact. Blue now closes the vertical sandwich, capturing both Yellow and Red; this eliminates Yellow and leaves Red one loss from elimination.
Yellow is now Void, so I’m using it as a durable positional blocker. Moving onto (4,3) secures a second central square for Team A while keeping (3,4) occupied and restricting Blue’s central mobility.

With both eliminated colors now limited to non-capturing Void moves, I’m repositioning Green toward the vacant lower-right center. From (4,6), it can occupy (4,4) next turn and strengthen our center while Blue hunts Red’s final loss.

I’m sealing Blue’s central piece on (3,3). After Blue’s move, Void Yellow should vacate (3,4) to (4,4); Red can then descend from (0,4) to (3,4), sandwiching Blue against Red on (3,2). That third Blue loss eliminates Team B.

Red has stepped beside our trapped central Blue. I’m creating a direct winning threat from below: Blue at (5,1) can rise to (3,1), sandwich Red at (3,2) against Blue at (3,3), and deliver Red’s third loss.

I’m following through on the elimination setup: Void Yellow vacates (3,4) for (4,4), opening Red’s path from (0,4). Red can then land on (3,4) and sandwich Blue at (3,3) against Red at (3,2), inflicting Blue’s third loss and winning by team elimination.
I’m using the edge Void to close Red’s upward escape at (2,2) while leaving Blue’s winning landing square at (3,1) open. Red’s advanced piece must now retreat through a narrower route or be captured.
I’m completing the prepared sandwich: Red lands on (3,4), capturing Blue at (3,3) against Red at (3,2). This is Blue’s third loss, eliminating Team B and winning the game.
